Getting started with readboj

Source: vignettes/readboj.Rmd
readboj.Rmd

readboj is an R client for official Bank of Japan (BOJ) statistics. It is designed for workflows where the source response, parser schema, and retrieval identity matter as much as the resulting values. The package can read exact API series, search metadata, inspect official bulk files, and discover dated Tankan comprehensive-data releases.

This article takes the shortest path to a useful result. Its default build combines a verified rendering made from an official API response with small synthetic fixtures that exercise the public parsers. Network retrieval remains an explicit opt-in, so vignette and CRAN builds stay deterministic and offline.

Load the package and discover databases 

databases <- boj_databases()
databases[c(1L, 12L, 40L), c("db", "category_en", "name_en")]
#>      db                          category_en
#> 1  IR01 Interest Rates on Deposits and Loans
#> 12 FM08                    Financial Markets
#> 40   CO                               TANKAN
#>                                          name_en
#> 1  The Basic Discount Rates and Basic Loan Rates
#> 12                        Foreign Exchange Rates
#> 40                                        TANKAN

boj_databases() is a local, revisioned registry. Its db values are the identities accepted by the API; the bilingual names and category are useful for presenting a choice to a user. The returned data frame also has provenance, including the BOJ API-manual URL and source hash:

db_provenance <- boj_provenance(databases)
db_provenance[c("source", "source_url", "manual_revision", "database_count")]
#> $source
#> [1] "Bank of Japan Time-Series Data Search API Manual"
#> 
#> $source_url
#> [1] "https://www.stat-search.boj.or.jp/info/api_manual_en.pdf"
#> 
#> $manual_revision
#> [1] "2026-02-18"
#> 
#> $database_count
#> [1] 50

Retrieve and chart a time series

The following workflow searches official metadata, selects the exact monthly exchange-rate series FM08/FXERM07, retrieves a closed 2025 period, keeps valid date and value rows, and charts the result. Set READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES=true to execute the bounded network path. The default article build displays the checked-in rendering made from the verified response recorded in inst/NOTICE/boj-chart-source.txt.

cache <- file.path(tempdir(), "readboj-chart-cache")
matches <- search_boj_series(
  query = "FXERM07", db = "FM08", language = "en", limit = 10L,
  cache_dir = cache, deadline = Sys.time() + 90
)
selected <- matches[matches$series_code == "FXERM07", , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(nrow(selected) == 1L)

series <- read_boj_series(
  db = selected$db[[1]], code = selected$series_code[[1]],
  start_date = "202501", end_date = "202512", language = "en",
  cache_dir = cache, deadline = Sys.time() + 90
)
chart_data <- series[
  !is.na(series$date) & is.finite(series$value),
  c("date", "value")
]
stopifnot(nrow(chart_data) > 1L)
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    chart_data,
    ggplot2::aes(x = date, y = value)
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line() +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = "Yen per U.S. dollar in 2025",
      subtitle = "Monthly published observations",
      x = "Month",
      y = "Yen per U.S. dollar",
      caption = "Source: Bank of Japan Time-Series Data Search API"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
}

The rendered series is US.Dollar/Yen Spot Rate at 17:00 in JST, Average in the Month, Tokyo Market, measured in yen per U.S. dollar. The chart is a readboj documentation illustration rather than an official BoJ chart or a bundled raw-data snapshot. Use boj_provenance(series) after a live run to retain the response URL, retrieval time, hashes, and query identity.

Parse and inspect a saved response

For a completely reproducible first success, parse an exact local response body with read_boj_snapshot(). This is the same normalised observation schema used by the API reader, without a live request:

observations <- read_boj_snapshot(
  fixture_file("api-data-page-1.json"),
  type = "data_json",
  db = "FM08"
)
observations[, c(
  "db", "series_code", "frequency", "period", "date",
  "value", "raw_value", "value_status"
)]
#>     db series_code frequency period       date  value raw_value value_status
#> 1 FM08    SYNTHM01   MONTHLY 202601 2026-01-01 101.25    101.25     observed
#> 2 FM08    SYNTHM01   MONTHLY 202602 2026-02-01     NA      <NA>         null
#> 3 FM08    SYNTHM01   MONTHLY 202603 2026-03-01 103.75    103.75     observed

The observation table keeps both the official period code and a parsed Date. value is numeric where a value is present; a JSON null remains an NA_real_, and value_status records that it was "null". The raw_value column is retained so a downstream transformation can distinguish a missing source value from a value that was never returned.

The result is an ordinary data frame with stable columns and a provenance attribute. Use boj_provenance() whenever a result is saved, joined, or reported:

observation_provenance <- boj_provenance(observations)
observation_provenance[c(
  "source", "raw_sha256", "semantic_sha256", "bytes",
  "parser_schema"
)]
#> $source
#> [1] "local response snapshot"
#> 
#> $raw_sha256
#> [1] "d40035a4d0847d5f9162f98468577f6dbec67545e032955b36d0aea8ac1ad3f3"
#> 
#> $semantic_sha256
#> [1] "c376b8ec04648c05b0ab73f2d400b36e21d52f29c92e9d693cceb6119d2e65c9"
#> 
#> $bytes
#> [1] 484
#> 
#> $parser_schema
#> [1] "1"
basename(observation_provenance$path)
#> [1] "api-data-page-1.json"

The raw SHA-256 identifies the exact response bytes. For JSON, the semantic hash is stable when only the volatile API DATE changes. This gives a small but useful audit trail even for a local fixture.

Reuse connected results offline

The retrieval shown in the chart workflow writes successful responses to its bounded cache_dir. Repeating the same read_boj_series() call with offline = TRUE replays a matching current snapshot without a network request. Requests use HTTPS and official BoJ hosts, and the public API requires no BoJ credentials. Typed readboj_* conditions distinguish unavailable sources, transport failures, invalid responses, and configured resource bounds.

For prescribed service wording and BOJ terms links, use:

credit <- boj_api_credit()
credit[c("credit", "api_notice", "copyright", "service_release_contact")]
#> $credit
#> [1] "This service uses the API provided by the \"Bank of Japan Time-Series Data Search.\" The Bank of Japan does not guarantee the content of the service."
#> 
#> $api_notice
#> [1] "https://www.stat-search.boj.or.jp/info/api_notice_en.pdf"
#> 
#> $copyright
#> [1] "https://www.boj.or.jp/en/about/copyright.htm"
#> 
#> $service_release_contact
#> [1] "post.rsd17@boj.or.jp"

The package handles parsing and source identity; users remain responsible for the BOJ service credit, release notification, and any downstream use of live data.
